subject: Procurement / payment constraints and next steps for OmniPay onboarding
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lewis <jordan.lewis@omnipay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: procurement / payment constraints and next steps

Thanks again for the demo time earlier, Jordan — appreciate you walking through OmniPay's AP flow. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on during the call: 

- Procurement posture: you said vendor onboarding and W-9 are required; marketplace purchasing is possible but procurement tends to prefer direct vendor relationships for tiered pricing.
- Payment method: preference depends on invoice size (you mentioned PO for larger engagements). We need to confirm the threshold and net terms.
- AP constraints: any card limits, signatory approvals, or tax docs we should expect?

Next steps (action owners):
1) Kimberly (me) — send our vendor packet + SOC2 summary (attached).
2) OmniPay (Jordan) — confirm PO threshold, required net terms, procurement contact, and return vendor_onboarding_form if possible.
3) Aditya/Marissa (cc) — will map our procurement checklist to OmniPay requirements and flag any integration/marketplace questions.

Attachments: vendor_packet.pdf (vendor packet, onboarding checklist)

If you can reply with the procurement contact and whether OmniPay prefers a PO-first flow or will accept card for pilots < $25k, that will help us scope the pilot agreement.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
(Attachment: vendor_packet.pdf, 280KB)

From: Jordan Lewis <jordan.lewis@omnipay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@omnipay.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T16:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement / payment constraints and next steps

Thanks, Kimberly — great recap. Quick answers from procurement: 

- PO vs card: OmniPay uses PO for recurring/one-off invoices > $30,000 and for any vendor requiring net-45 / net-60 terms. For pilots or one-off purchases under $30k we can typically pay via corporate card or an AP push.
- Net terms: standard review is net-30; exceptions to net-45/60 require VP finance sign-off (normally a 7–10 business-day approval window).
- Required docs: W-9, vendor onboarding form, and a copy of the vendor's SOC2 summary if you have one. E-invoicing (Peppol) is not in use; we accept emailed invoices to ap@omnipay.com.
- Marketplace: procurement prefers direct vendor contracts for strategic integrations; marketplace purchases are allowed but procurement will often block marketplace SKUs for SOW-style engagements.

I've attached the vendor onboarding form — Ellen is our procurement lead (ellen.park@omnipay.com) and will own the setup. I'll loop Finance on the deal once we align on the payment method.

Jordan
Head of Strategic Procurement | OmniPay Solutions
jordan.lewis@omnipay.com
(Attachment: vendor_onboarding_form.pdf, 120KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: procurement / payment constraints and next steps

Forwarding Jordan's note and adding a few internal clarifications so we can prepare the right path: 

- PO threshold: Jordan says > $30k => PO preferred. For pilots we should propose a 3-month pilot on card (if under $30k) or a short-term PO with net-30 if they want vendor visibility.
- Approvals: if they ask for net-45/60 we need to set expectation of VP finance approval; suggest we keep standard net-30 in the SOW and provide a fallback commit for net-45 only after executive review.
- Marketplace vs direct: since procurement prefers direct contracts for integrations, let's surface the marketplace option as fallback only (it helps with fast procurement but limits custom SSO / data routing).

Questions for OmniPay to close in the next email:
- Can Ellen confirm the PO threshold in writing and provide the vendor template?
- Who signs on OmniPay's side for pilot SOWs (procurement or legal)?
- Any card processor / invoice descriptor requirements we should include on invoices to avoid holds?

I'll draft a short mutual action plan once we hear back from Ellen/Jordan.

—Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lewis <jordan.lewis@omnipay.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@omnipay.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement / payment constraints and next steps — mutual action plan

Thanks, Jordan + Ellen — appreciate the details. Per our internal discussion, here's a short mutual action plan to keep momentum: 

1) Today (OmniPay / Ellen): confirm PO threshold and share OmniPay vendor template + any specific invoice descriptor requirements (action: Ellen).
2) 2027-04-23 (Redwood / Kimberly + Aditya): send a 90-day pilot SOW (we will default net-30) and provide a sample invoice (attached).
3) 2027-04-26 (OmniPay): procurement sends vendor setup confirmation and expected timeline to go live (ap@omnipay.com copied).
4) 2027-04-30 (Both): kickoff scheduled if vendor onboarding completed.

Attachments from our side: SOC2-summary.pdf (one-page), sample-invoice.csv (example line item format).

If you confirm the PO threshold and whether a card payment is acceptable for a sub-$30k pilot, we will prepare the SOW and get legal to pre-clear our invoice descriptor to avoid AP holds.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
(Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf, sample-invoice.csv)
